proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(m\in\mathcal M_n(B)\) and a block \(B_l\).  By
\(\mathrm{def{:}observed\text{-}block\text{-}means}\),
\[
 \overline Y_l^{\mathrm{obs}}(D)
 =\frac1{r_l}\sum_{i\in B_l}Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}.
\tag{11}
\]
The partition is known by \(\mathrm{ass{:}partition}\), and every
coordinate \(Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}\) is contained in \(D\); hence the
finite sum (11) is \(\sigma(D)\)-measurable.  If \(A_l=1\), then all
assignments in \(B_l\) equal one.  By
\(\mathrm{ass{:}block\text{-}exposure}\), \(e_i(Z)=a\) for every
\(i\in B_l\), and observed-outcome consistency in the definition of
\(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}\) gives \(Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}=Y_i(a)\).
Therefore, by \(\mathrm{def{:}block\text{-}means}\),
\[
 \overline Y_l^{\mathrm{obs}}(D)
 =\frac1{r_l}\sum_{i\in B_l}Y_i(a)=\mu_l(a).
\]
The same argument with all assignments equal to zero shows that
\(C_l=1\) implies
\(\overline Y_l^{\mathrm{obs}}(D)=\mu_l(b)\).
The fixed-schedule assumption ensures that the right sides are
nonrandom under \(P_Z\), and boundedness ensures all displayed finite
averages exist.

For a fixed block \(B_l\), balanced independent assignment gives every
one of its \(2^{r_l}\) binary patterns probability \(2^{-r_l}\).
Exactly one pattern is all treated and exactly one is all controlled.
Thus, by the definitions of \(A_l,C_l,H_l\),
\[
 P_Z(A_l=1)=q_l,\qquad P_Z(C_l=1)=q_l,\qquad
 P_Z(H_l=1)=1-2q_l,
\tag{12}
\]
and \(A_lC_l=0\) pointwise.  Distinct triples depend on disjoint
coordinates of \(Z\) by \(\mathrm{ass{:}partition}\), so
\(\mathrm{ass{:}balanced\text{-}bernoulli}\) makes them independent
across \(l\).

On \(A_l=1\) and \(C_l=1\), respectively,
\(\mathrm{lem{:}observed\text{-}block\text{-}means}\) identifies the
reported block mean with \(\mu_l(a)\) and \(\mu_l(b)\).  Hence the
definition of \(X_l\) may be written, on all assignments, as
\[
 X_l=\frac{w_l}{q_l}\{A_l\mu_l(a)-C_l\mu_l(b)\}.
\tag{13}
\]
Using (12), mutual exclusion, and the fixedness of the two means,
\[
 \mathbb E_ZX_l
 =w_l\{\mu_l(a)-\mu_l(b)\},
\tag{14}
\]
and
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{Var}_Z(X_l)
 &\le\mathbb E_ZX_l^2\\
 &=\frac{w_l^2}{q_l}
   \{\mu_l(a)^2+\mu_l(b)^2\}\\
 &\le\frac{w_l^2}{2q_l}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{15}
\]
The last inequality uses
\(\mathrm{ass{:}bounded\text{-}outcomes}\), which implies
\(|\mu_l(a)|,|\mu_l(b)|\le1/2\).  Summing (15) gives
\[
 \sum_l\operatorname{Var}_Z(X_l)\le
 \frac12\sum_l\frac{w_l^2}{q_l}=\frac S2.
\tag{16}
\]

It remains to verify the almost-sure increment bound rather than infer
it from the second moment.  Equation (13) shows
\(|X_l|\le w_l/(2q_l)\), whereas (14) and boundedness give
\(|\mathbb EX_l|\le w_l\).  Since \(q_l\le1/2\),
\[
 |X_l-\mathbb EX_l|
 \le\frac{w_l}{2q_l}+w_l
 \le\frac{w_l}{q_l}\le M.
\tag{17}
\]
For the smallest unequal stress test, take one singleton and one
two-unit block.  The \(2\cdot4=8\) assignments give categorical counts
\((1,1,0)\) and \((1,1,2)\) in the two blocks, respectively; dividing
by \(2\) and \(4\) reproduces (12), and direct summation of the three
possible values in (13) reproduces (14)--(17).  Thus no assignment in
that exhaustive instance contradicts the reduction.

Fix \(m\in\mathcal M_n(B)\), put
\[
 W_l=X_l-\mathbb E_ZX_l,\qquad z=\log(2/\alpha).
\]
By \(\mathrm{lem{:}block\text{-}reduction}\), the \(W_l\) are
independent and centered,
\[
 \sum_l\mathbb EW_l^2\le S/2,\qquad |W_l|\le M.
\tag{18}
\]
Apply \(\mathrm{lem{:}finite\text{-}product\text{-}exponential}\)
with \(v=\sum_l\mathbb EW_l^2\), \(c=M\), and the displayed \(z\).
The threshold in that lemma is nondecreasing in \(v\), so (18) gives
\[
 P_Z\!\left\{\left|\sum_lW_l\right|>
 \sqrt{S\log(2/\alpha)}
 +\frac M3\log(2/\alpha)\right\}\le\alpha.
\tag{19}
\]
Equations (14) and the definition of \(\theta\) give
\[
 \sum_l\mathbb E_ZX_l
 =\sum_lw_l\{\mu_l(a)-\mu_l(b)\}=\theta.
\tag{20}
\]
Since \(\widehat\theta=\sum_lX_l\), (19)--(20) imply
\[
 P_{Z,m}\{|\widehat\theta-\theta|\le h_\alpha\}\ge1-\alpha.
\tag{21}
\]
The statistic is measurable solely from \(D\) by
\(\mathrm{def{:}block\text{-}ht}\) and
\(\mathrm{lem{:}observed\text{-}block\text{-}means}\); \(S,M,\alpha\)
are known design quantities.  Boundedness yields
\(\mu_l(a)-\mu_l(b)\in[-1,1]\), and \(\sum_lw_l=1\) follows from the
partition, so \(\theta\in[-1,1]\).  Consequently, on the event in
(21), intersecting
\([\widehat\theta-h_\alpha,\widehat\theta+h_\alpha]\) with
\([-1,1]\) cannot remove \(\theta\).  This proves coverage.  Finally,
the length of an intersection is bounded by the length of either
interval:
\[
 \operatorname{len}(I_{\mathrm{HT},\alpha})
 \le\min\{2,2h_\alpha\}
 =2\min\!\left\{1,\sqrt{S\log(2/\alpha)}
 +\frac M3\log(2/\alpha)\right\}.
\]
This bound is deterministic and therefore holds on every assignment,
including the exhaustive unequal three-unit stress test described in
\(\mathrm{lem{:}block\text{-}reduction}\).

For fixed \(v\), the schedule in
\(\mathrm{def{:}hard\text{-}subexperiment\text{-}embedding}\) is a
nonrandom array, so it satisfies
\(\mathrm{ass{:}fixed\text{-}schedule}\).  Its entries are either
\(v_l\in\{-1/2,1/2\}\) or zero, so it satisfies
\(\mathrm{ass{:}bounded\text{-}outcomes}\).  It uses the fixed design,
partition, and exposure map from the model class, hence \(m_v\in
\mathcal M_n(B)\).  Direct substitution in
\(\mathrm{def{:}block\text{-}means}\) gives
\[
 \mu_l^v(a)=v_l,\qquad \mu_l^v(b)=0,
\]
and therefore
\[
 \theta(m_v)=\sum_lw_l\{\mu_l^v(a)-\mu_l^v(b)\}
 =\sum_lw_lv_l=T(v).
\tag{22}
\]

By the block exposure rule, an outcome in \(B_l\) equals \(v_l\)
exactly on the all-treated pattern and equals zero on every other
pattern.  Thus
\[
 K_l=A_l=\mathbf1\{Z_{B_l}=\mathbf1_{B_l}\},\qquad
 Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}=K_lv_l\quad(i\in B_l),
\tag{23}
\]
and \(O_l=(K_l,K_lv_l)\) is measurable from \(D\).  The block
assignments are independent.  Within a block all \(2^{r_l}\) patterns
have equal probability, whence
\[
 \operatorname{Law}(Z_{B_l}\mid K_l=1)
 =\delta_{\mathbf1_{B_l}},\qquad
 \operatorname{Law}(Z_{B_l}\mid K_l=0)
 =\operatorname{Uniform}
 \bigl(\{0,1\}^{B_l}\setminus\{\mathbf1_{B_l}\}\bigr).
\tag{24}
\]
This proves both the stated Bernoulli law of \(K_l\) and the product
conditional kernel \(\bigotimes_l\nu_{l,k_l}\).  In particular, (24)
retains the all-control assignment together with all mixed patterns;
none is discarded as ancillary.

For completeness, the randomization devices in the construction may
be realized explicitly.  Outside the null set of dyadic rationals,
write the binary digits of \(R\), and distribute successive digits
cyclically among \(L+1\) coordinates.  Independent fair binary digits
show on every dyadic cylinder that the resulting coordinates
\((R_0,\ldots,R_L)\) have product Lebesgue law; extension from
cylinders gives the asserted pushforward, and arbitrary values on the
null exceptional set preserve it.  Because each \(\nu_{l,k}\) has
finite support, \(F_l(k,\cdot)\) can be its inverse-distribution
sampler and is measurable.

Under \(Q_t\), \(K_l\) are independent Bernoulli variables with
probabilities \(q_l\), and the split coordinates are independent
uniforms.  Equations (24) and the definition of \(F_l\) therefore give,
conditional on \(V=v\),
\[
 \operatorname{Law}(Z^*\mid K=k,V=v)
 =\bigotimes_l\nu_{l,k_l}
 =\operatorname{Law}_{Z,m_v}(Z\mid K=k).
\tag{25}
\]
Equations (23) and (25) imply
\[
 \operatorname{Law}(D^*,R_0\mid V=v)
 =\operatorname{Law}_{Z,R_0,m_v}(D,R_0).
\tag{26}
\]
Composition of the measurable samplers with a measurable
\(\Gamma\) proves measurability of \(\Lambda_\Gamma\).
Because (22) identifies the two fixed targets and (26) identifies the
entire randomized observations, it follows that
\[
\begin{aligned}
 P_{K,R}\{T(v)\in\Lambda_\Gamma(O,R)\mid V=v\}
 &=P_{Z,R_0,m_v}\{\theta(m_v)\in\Gamma(D,R_0)\},\\
 \mathbb E_{K,R}[\operatorname{len}\{\Lambda_\Gamma(O,R)\}\mid V=v]
 &=\mathbb E_{Z,R_0,m_v}[\operatorname{len}\{\Gamma(D,R_0)\}].
\end{aligned}
\tag{27}
\]

If \(\Gamma\in\mathfrak C_\alpha\), its pointwise honesty applied to
each \(m_v\) makes the first line of (27) at least \(1-\alpha\).
Integrating that inequality over \(V\sim\pi_t\), using nonnegativity
and Tonelli's theorem, gives
\[
 Q_t\{T(V)\in\Lambda_\Gamma(O,R)\}\ge1-\alpha.
\tag{28}
\]
Similarly, the second line of (27) and the fact that a prior average
does not exceed a supremum give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \sup_{m'\in\mathcal M_n(B)}
 \mathbb E_{Z,R,m'}\operatorname{len}\{\Gamma(D,R)\}
 &\ge\sup_v\mathbb E_{K,R}
 [\operatorname{len}\{\Lambda_\Gamma(O,R)\}\mid V=v]\\
 &\ge\mathbb E_{Q_t}
 \operatorname{len}\{\Lambda_\Gamma(O,R)\}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{29}
\]
This proves every asserted bridge statement.  Equations (28)--(29)
use no posterior-spread claim; such a claim would be a separate lower
bound in the weighted-erasure experiment.

Fix a deterministic subset \(J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,L\}\) and define
\[
 \widehat\theta_J=\sum_{l\in J}X_l,\qquad
 \theta_J=\sum_{l\in J}w_l\{\mu_l(a)-\mu_l(b)\},
\]
\[
 S_J=\sum_{l\in J}\frac{w_l^2}{q_l},\qquad
 M_J=\max_{l\in J}\frac{w_l}{q_l},\qquad
 b_J=\sum_{l\notin J}w_l,
\]
with \(M_\varnothing=0\).  The block reduction gives independent
centered variables \(W_l=X_l-\mathbb EX_l\), for \(l\in J\), satisfying
\[
 \sum_{l\in J}\mathbb EW_l^2\le S_J/2,\qquad |W_l|\le M_J.
\tag{30}
\]
The finite-product exponential calculation proved for the full
estimator in \(\mathrm{thm{:}finite\text{-}upper}\) applies verbatim to
this finite subproduct: equations (1)--(3) depend only on independence,
centering, the variance sum, and the displayed increment bound.  Thus,
with \(y=\log(2/\alpha)\),
\[
 P_Z\!\left\{|\widehat\theta_J-\theta_J|>
 \sqrt{S_Jy}+\frac{M_J}{3}y\right\}\le\alpha.
\tag{31}
\]
Bounded outcomes imply
\[
 |\theta-\theta_J|
 =\left|\sum_{l\notin J}w_l\{\mu_l(a)-\mu_l(b)\}\right|
 \le b_J.
\tag{32}
\]
Consequently the observed-data interval
\[
 I_J(D)=[-1,1]\cap
 \left[\widehat\theta_J-b_J-\sqrt{S_Jy}-\frac{M_Jy}{3},
       \widehat\theta_J+b_J+\sqrt{S_Jy}+\frac{M_Jy}{3}\right]
\tag{33}
\]
has coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) by (31)--(32).  It is measurable
from \(D\), since each \(X_l\) is, and its length is at most
\[
 2\min\!\left\{1,b_J+\sqrt{S_Jy}+\frac{M_Jy}{3}\right\}.
\tag{34}
\]
There are finitely many subsets.  Choose, using a fixed deterministic
tie rule, a minimizer of the known design expression in (34).
The selected \(J\) is nonrandom, so (31) retains its coverage, and
the expression minimized is exactly
\(\rho_\alpha(w,q)\) from
\(\mathrm{def{:}trimmed\text{-}radius}\).  Equations (33)--(34)
therefore furnish an element of \(\mathfrak C_\alpha\) having the
claimed length.

For each size-one block,
\[
 (w_l,q_l)=\left(\frac1{12},\frac12\right),\qquad
 \frac{w_l}{q_l}=\frac16,
\]
whereas for each size-three block,
\[
 (w_l,q_l)=\left(\frac14,\frac18\right),\qquad
 \frac{w_l}{q_l}=2.
\tag{35}
\]
At \(\alpha=1/4\), the quadratic budget is \(x=\log4\).
The water-filling certificate in
\(\mathrm{lem{:}capped\text{-}trimming\text{-}duality}\) shows that a
candidate capping the three size-three coordinates and leaving the
three size-one coordinates uncapped must satisfy
\[
 3\left(\frac18\right)
 +3\left(\frac12\right)\left(\frac{\lambda_\alpha}{6}\right)^2
 =\log4.
\]
Hence
\[
 \lambda_\alpha=\sqrt{24(\log4-3/8)}.
\tag{36}
\]
Numerically, \(1/2<\lambda_\alpha<6\), so the three coordinates with
breakpoint \(q_l/w_l=1/2\) are indeed capped and the three with
breakpoint \(6\) are indeed uncapped.  Substitution in the linear
objective gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \omega_{1/4}
 &=3\left(\frac14\right)
 +3\left(\frac1{12}\right)\frac{\lambda_\alpha}{6}\\
 &=\frac34+\sqrt{\frac{\log4-3/8}{24}}
 \approx0.9553.
\end{aligned}
\tag{37}
\]
For \(\rho_0\), retain only the three size-one blocks.  Their omitted
weight is \(3/4\), and their quadratic contribution is
\[
 \sum_{l\in J}\frac{w_l^2}{q_l}
 =3\frac{(1/12)^2}{1/2}=\frac1{24}.
\]
Therefore
\[
 \rho_0\le\frac34+\frac1{\sqrt{24}}\approx0.9541,
\]
as asserted.

Assume first that \(G\) is the disjoint union of the clique components
\(B_1,\ldots,B_L\).  Then \(N_G[i]=B_l\) for every \(i\in B_l\).
By \(\mathrm{def{:}package\text{-}label\text{-}maps}\), for every such
\(i\),
\[
\begin{array}{c|cc}
 &a&b\\ \hline
 L^{\mathrm{pkg}}_{i,\cdot}&A_l&1-A_l\\
 L^{\mathrm{ref}}_{i,\cdot}&A_l&C_l .
\end{array}
\tag{38}
\]
The first columns always agree.  Therefore the matrices agree if and
only if \(1-A_l=C_l\) for every block, equivalently
\[
 A_l+C_l=1\quad\text{for every }l.
\tag{39}
\]
The block reduction gives \(A_lC_l=0\) and
\(H_l=1-A_l-C_l\).  Thus (39) fails exactly when some block is mixed.
For a mixed block, (38) supplies the explicit coordinate witness:
the package second column is one, while the reference All Control
column is zero.

The remaining assertions follow by evaluating the branches of
\(\mathrm{def{:}software\text{-}diagnostic}\) in their prescribed
order.  On a clique graph the neighborhood test passes.  The diagnostic
then independently checks each supplied output against its defining
map and checks (38).  When all checks pass, it computes the block means
from \(D\), and balanced assignment gives
\(q_l=2^{-r_l}\); the displayed definitions then determine
\(w_l,S,M,\omega_\alpha,\rho_\alpha\), and
\(I_{\mathrm{HT},\alpha}\) exactly.  The finite-upper and trimmed-upper
theorems certify the reported confidence constructions.  When (38)
fails, its first unequal coordinate is returned and the confidence
output is suppressed.

Finally, if some \(N_G[i]\ne B_l\) for \(i\in B_l\), the first branch
of the diagnostic fires before any label comparison.  A crossing
neighbor witnesses overlap between purported components; a missing
within-block neighbor witnesses noncliqueness.  In either case the
definition returns \(\texttt{graph-reject}\) and no interval.  These
cases are disjoint from the valid-clique label-mismatch branch, proving
the complete diagnostic claim.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(W_1,\ldots,W_{N_0}\) be independent, centered random variables with \(|W_j|\le c\), and put \(v=\sum_j\mathbb E W_j^2\). For every \(z>0\),
\[
 \Pr\!\left\{\left|\sum_jW_j\right|>
 \sqrt{2vz}+\frac{cz}{3}\right\}\le 2e^{-z}.
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
If \(c=0\), then every \(W_j=0\) almost surely and the assertion is immediate.  Suppose \(c>0\).  For \(\lambda\ge0\) and \(u\le1\), the elementary Bennett inequality
\[
 e^{\lambda c u}\le
 1+\lambda c u+
 \{e^{\lambda c}-1-\lambda c\}u^2
\tag{1}
\]
holds when \(|u|\le1\).  Indeed, after the affine tangent at zero is subtracted, differentiation shows that
\[
 u\longmapsto\frac{e^{\lambda c u}-1-\lambda c u}{u^2},
\]
with its continuous value at zero, is maximized on \([-1,1]\) at \(u=1\).  Apply (1) with \(u=W_j/c\), use \(\mathbb EW_j=0\), and then \(1+a\le e^a\).  This gives
\[
 \log\mathbb E e^{\lambda W_j}
 \le \frac{\mathbb EW_j^2}{c^2}
       \{e^{\lambda c}-1-\lambda c\}.
\tag{2}
\]
Independence and Markov's inequality therefore imply, for every \(u>0\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \Pr\!\left\{\sum_jW_j\ge u\right\}
 &\le\inf_{\lambda>0}
 \exp\!\left[-\lambda u+\frac v{c^2}
       \{e^{\lambda c}-1-\lambda c\}\right]  \\
 &=\exp\!\left[-\frac v{c^2}
 h\!\left(\frac{cu}{v}\right)\right],
 \qquad h(y)=(1+y)\log(1+y)-y ,
\end{aligned}
\tag{3}
\]
where, when \(v>0\), equality follows by choosing
\(\lambda=c^{-1}\log(1+cu/v)\).  If \(v=0\), centering and
\(\sum_j\mathbb EW_j^2=0\) imply \(W_j=0\) almost surely for every
\(j\), so that case is already settled.

It remains to invert (3).  For \(a\ge0\), put
\(y(a)=\sqrt{2a}+a/3\).  Writing \(b=\sqrt{2a}\), differentiation gives
\[
 \frac{d}{db}\{h(b+b^2/6)-b^2/2\}
 =\left(1+\frac b3\right)\log(1+b+b^2/6)-b .
\]
The last expression is nonnegative because
\[
 \log(1+b+b^2/6)-\frac{3b}{3+b}\ge0,
\]
and the derivative of its left side equals
\[
 \frac{2(3+b)}{b^2+6b+6}-\frac9{(3+b)^2}
 =\frac{b^2(2b+9)}
 {(b^2+6b+6)(3+b)^2}\ge0,
\]
while its value at \(b=0\) is zero.  Hence \(h(y(a))\ge a\).
Taking \(a=c^2z/v\) and
\(u=\sqrt{2vz}+cz/3\) in (3) proves that the upper-tail probability
is at most \(e^{-z}\).  The same calculation applies to \(-W_j\);
the union bound proves the displayed two-sided inequality.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(0<\alpha\le1/4\), \(x=\log(1/\alpha)\), and \(y=\log(2/\alpha)\).  The optimizer in \(\mathrm{def{:}capped\text{-}modulus}\) is the stated water-filling vector.  Moreover,
\[
 \omega_\alpha(w,q)\le\rho_\alpha(w,q)\le4\omega_\alpha(w,q),
 \qquad
 \omega_1(w,q)\le\rho_0(w,q)\le3\omega_1(w,q),
\]
where \(\omega_1\) denotes the same capped program with quadratic budget one.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
All weights and reveal probabilities are positive, and the feasible set
\[
 {\cal D}_z=\left\{\delta\in[0,1]^L:
                 \sum_lq_l\delta_l^2\le z\right\}
\]
is compact, so a maximizer exists.  If \(z\ge\sum_lq_l\), the coordinatewise
largest feasible vector is \(\delta_l=1\), and positivity of \(w_l\)
makes it optimal.  Suppose \(0<z<\sum_lq_l\).  The function
\[
 f(\lambda)=\sum_lq_l\min\{1,\lambda w_l/q_l\}^2
\]
is continuous, equals zero at \(\lambda=0\), is strictly increasing
until it reaches \(\sum_lq_l\), and then is constant.  Thus there is a
unique \(\lambda>0\) before the terminal plateau for which \(f(\lambda)=z\).
Put
\[
 \delta_l^*=\min\{1,\lambda w_l/q_l\}.
\tag{4}
\]
For any \(\delta\in{\cal D}_z\), let \(C=\{l:\delta_l^*=1\}\) and
\(J=C^c\).  If \(l\in J\), then \(w_l=q_l\delta_l^*/\lambda\), and
\[
 w_l(\delta_l-\delta_l^*)
 \le\frac{q_l}{2\lambda}(\delta_l^2-(\delta_l^*)^2).
\tag{5}
\]
If \(l\in C\), then \(w_l\ge q_l/\lambda\), while
\(\delta_l-1\le0\); consequently
\[
 w_l(\delta_l-1)
 \le\frac{q_l}{\lambda}(\delta_l-1)
 \le\frac{q_l}{2\lambda}(\delta_l^2-1).
\tag{6}
\]
Summing (5)--(6) and using both quadratic constraints gives
\[
 \sum_lw_l(\delta_l-\delta_l^*)
 \le\frac1{2\lambda}
 \sum_lq_l\{\delta_l^2-(\delta_l^*)^2\}\le0.
\]
Thus (4) is the global maximizer.  This is also a complete
Karush--Kuhn--Tucker certificate; no differentiability at a cap is needed.

We next prove the trimming comparison.  For every feasible \(\delta\)
at budget \(x\) and every subset \(J_0\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \sum_lw_l\delta_l
 &\le \sum_{l\notin J_0}w_l+
      \sum_{l\in J_0}w_l\delta_l\\
 &\le \sum_{l\notin J_0}w_l+
 \left(\sum_{l\in J_0}\frac{w_l^2}{q_l}\right)^{1/2}
 \left(\sum_{l\in J_0}q_l\delta_l^2\right)^{1/2}\\
 &\le \sum_{l\notin J_0}w_l+
 \sqrt{x\sum_{l\in J_0}w_l^2/q_l}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{7}
\]
Because \(y\ge x\), taking first the supremum over \(\delta\) and then
the infimum over \(J_0\) proves
\(\omega_\alpha\le\rho_\alpha\).

For the reverse inequality, the all-capped case gives
\(\rho_\alpha\le\sum_lw_l=\omega_\alpha\) by choosing
\(J_0=\varnothing\).  Otherwise apply (4) at budget \(x\), and retain
the uncapped set \(J\).  Define
\[
 A=\sum_{l\in J}\frac{w_l^2}{q_l},\qquad
 Q_C=\sum_{l\in C}q_l,\qquad B=\sum_{l\in C}w_l.
\]
The active constraint and the value of the objective are
\[
 x=Q_C+\lambda^2A,\qquad
 \omega_\alpha=B+\lambda A.
\tag{8}
\]
The cap inequalities give \(B\ge Q_C/\lambda\), so (8) yields
\[
 \omega_\alpha\ge\frac{x}{\lambda},\qquad
 A\le\frac{x}{\lambda^2},\qquad
 \max_{l\in J}\frac{w_l}{q_l}<\frac1\lambda.
\tag{9}
\]
Since \(x\ge\log4\), one has \(y=x+\log2\le3x/2\).
Choosing \(J_0=J\) in the definition of \(\rho_\alpha\), and applying
(8)--(9), gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \rho_\alpha
 &\le B+\sqrt{yA}+\frac y3\max_{l\in J}\frac{w_l}{q_l}\\
 &\le B+\sqrt{\frac32}\,\frac x\lambda+
       \frac12\,\frac x\lambda\\
 &\le\left(1+\sqrt{\frac32}+\frac12\right)\omega_\alpha
 <4\omega_\alpha.
\end{aligned}
\tag{10}
\]

Finally repeat (7) with quadratic budget one to get
\(\omega_1\le\rho_0\).  If \(\sum_lq_l\le1\), both are bounded as
\(\rho_0\le1=\omega_1\).  Otherwise (8)--(9), with \(x=1\), give
\[
 \rho_0\le B+\sqrt A\le B+\lambda^{-1}
 \le2\omega_1\le3\omega_1.
\]
This completes both the optimizer certificate and the two trimming
comparisons.

proposed.statement: For every \(0<\alpha\le1/4\) and every \(m\in\mathcal M_n(B)\), the interval \(I_{\mathrm{HT},\alpha}(D)\), which is a measurable function solely of \(D\) and known design quantities, obeys \(P_{Z,m}\{\theta\in I_{\mathrm{HT},\alpha}(D)\}\ge1-\alpha\) and \(\operatorname{len}\{I_{\mathrm{HT},\alpha}(D)\}\le2\min\{1,\sqrt{S\log(2/\alpha)}+(M/3)\log(2/\alpha)\}\).
proposed.justification: This is a genuinely reportable finite-sample interval: no latent block mean appears in the statistic or its endpoints.
proposed.gap: TchetgenTchetgenVanderWeele2012, Section 4.3, gives Hoeffding intervals for four binary two-stage partial-interference effects, and RigdonHudgens2015 inverts randomization tests for those effects under stratified interference. Their designs and estimands differ from the observed-data All Treat versus All Control interval under fixed independent assignment on unequal cliques.
proposed.consumer: An analyst using full-neighborhood exposures obtains a computable finite-sample interval and sees when a single rare block controls length.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Wire the proved finite-product exponential inequality into the unchanged finite-sample confidence theorem, as required by the orchestrator.

proposed.statement: For the unequal six-block population with \(r=(1,1,1,3,3,3)\), \(n=12\), and \(\alpha=1/4\), the three size-three coordinates cap and the three size-one coordinates do not. Explicitly, \(\lambda_\alpha=\sqrt{24(\log4-3/8)}\), \(\omega_{1/4}=3/4+\sqrt{(\log4-3/8)/24}\approx0.9553\), and the subset retaining only size-one blocks gives \(\rho_0\le3/4+1/\sqrt{24}\approx0.9541\).
proposed.justification: The numerical exhibit exposes the cap threshold and the near-matching trimming certificate in a reproducible unequal-block instance.
proposed.gap: An equal-block substitution has only one breakpoint and therefore cannot reproduce simultaneous capped and uncapped coordinates.
proposed.consumer: The software diagnostic uses this instance as a unit test for sorting, multiplier solution, and trimming output.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Wire the proved water-filling and trimming certificate into the unchanged numerical exhibit, as required by the orchestrator.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Prove the posterior-spread implication for the tilted weighted-erasure experiment uniformly over the stated conventional confidence levels and no-dominance arrays.
open_obligations.obstruction: The bridge to randomized original-data procedures is proved, but the current primitives do not supply the required biased weighted-Rademacher concentration-function estimate or the posterior missed-mass lower bound.
open_obligations.attempted: The likelihood-score and random-information route was audited. The orchestrator requires separate control of the exact factors \(1-t^2s_l^2\), compact tilt boundaries, and both conditional-noise regimes; those steps cannot be replaced by the previously rejected repeated-step argument.
open_obligations.partial_result: The tilted family is interior under the displayed no-dominance condition, and \(\mathrm{lem{:}hard\text{-}subexperiment\text{-}embedding}\) transfers pointwise coverage and expected length for every externally randomized rule.  What remains is the posterior-spread inequality itself: a future proof must establish a biased weighted-Rademacher concentration-function bound with conditional variances \(\sum_{K_l=0}w_l^2(1-t^2s_l^2)/4\), control compact-support endpoints, and compute posterior missed mass in both the small-conditional-noise and large-conditional-noise regimes.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The universal lower bound on worst-case expected length.
open_obligations.obstruction: Its declared lower-bound dependency, \(\mathrm{oeq{:}weighted\text{-}erasure\text{-}spread}\), remains unresolved by directive.
open_obligations.attempted: The finite upper bound and the exact randomized-decision embedding were completed; the remaining implication is precisely the posterior-spread step rather than another reduction.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The upper half is proved.  Put \(x=\log(1/\alpha)\) and \(y=\log(2/\alpha)\le3x/2\).  Under \(M\sqrt{x}\le c_0\sqrt S\), \(\mathrm{thm{:}finite\text{-}upper}\) gives
\[
 \mathcal R_\alpha(w,q)\le
 2\min\{1,(\sqrt{3/2}+c_0/2)\sqrt{Sx}\}
 \le C_1\min\{1,\sqrt{Sx}\}
\]
for a universal \(C_1\).  The hard-subexperiment bridge also reduces the desired all-procedure lower half exactly to \(\mathrm{oeq{:}weighted\text{-}erasure\text{-}spread}\).  No lower bound is claimed until that posterior-spread assertion is proved.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Prove the matching unrestricted minimax lower bound \(\mathcal R_\alpha\gtrsim\omega_\alpha\) for all measurable externally randomized intervals.
open_obligations.obstruction: The finite optimization and trimming duality are proved, but a capped perturbation by itself does not establish posterior interval spread under moving-support erasure laws.
open_obligations.attempted: The KKT optimizer, no-cap formula, trimming comparison, and minimax upper bound were closed. Per directive, the remaining route must separately prove the smooth-location erasure lower bound, endpoint control, and the likelihood or Hellinger-to-posterior-spread conversion.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The optimizer and trimming side are closed by \(\mathrm{lem{:}capped\text{-}trimming\text{-}duality}\):
\[
 \omega_\alpha\le\rho_\alpha\le4\omega_\alpha.
\]
Together with \(\mathrm{thm{:}trimmed\text{-}upper}\), this proves the unrestricted upper bound \(\mathcal R_\alpha\le8\omega_\alpha\).  If no cap binds, the active constraint gives \(\lambda_\alpha^2S=x_\alpha\) and hence \(\omega_\alpha=\lambda_\alpha S=\sqrt{Sx_\alpha}\).  The unproved part is the matching lower bound for all measurable externally randomized intervals; it requires the directed smooth-location erasure argument with explicit moving-support endpoint and posterior-spread control.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Prove that vanishing minimax expected length forces the capped modulus to vanish.
open_obligations.obstruction: That reverse implication is a direct consequence of the still-open global water-filling lower bound and cannot be obtained from the proved upper intervals.
open_obligations.attempted: The equivalence of the two computable moduli, the sufficient risk implication, and a valid clique-array witness showing that \(S\to0\) is not necessary were proved.
open_obligations.partial_result:
For fixed \(\alpha\), write \(x=\log(1/\alpha)>1\), and let \(\omega_z\) denote the capped program with budget \(z\).  Monotonicity and rescaling of feasible vectors give
\[
 \omega_1\le\omega_x\le\sqrt{x}\,\omega_1.
\]
Indeed, an optimizer at budget \(x\), divided by \(\sqrt x\), remains in \([0,1]^L\) and is feasible at budget one.  The proved trimming duality gives
\[
 \omega_1\le\rho_0\le3\omega_1,
\]
so \(\omega_\alpha\to0\) if and only if \(\rho_0\to0\).  The trimmed upper bound and confidence-level duality also give
\(\mathcal R_\alpha\le8\omega_\alpha\), proving
\(\omega_\alpha\to0\Longrightarrow\mathcal R_\alpha\to0\).
Conversely, \(\mathcal R_\alpha\to0\Longrightarrow\omega_\alpha\to0\)
is exactly the unresolved all-procedure erasure lower bound.

The last sentence about \(S\) is already certified independently of
that converse.  Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\(\omega_\alpha\le\sqrt{xS}\), so \(S\to0\) is sufficient.  It is not
necessary: for \(k\ge1\), take one block of size \(2k\), let
\(n_k=2k\,2^k\), and partition all remaining units into singletons.
The large block has \(w=2^{-k}\), \(q=2^{-2k}\), and contribution one
to \(S\); the singleton contribution is
\(2(n_k-2k)/n_k^2\to0\).  Hence \(S\to1\), while trimming the large
block gives \(\rho_\alpha\to0\) and therefore
\(\mathcal R_\alpha\to0\).

open_obligations.what_is_open: Certify the claimed two-sided minimax length order.
open_obligations.obstruction: The exact arithmetic and the upper rate close, but the minimax assertion invokes the unresolved lower half of \(\mathrm{thm{:}no\text{-}dominance\text{-}frontier}\).
open_obligations.attempted: Both exposure strata, \(S\), \(M\), the dominance ratio, and the distinct water-filling breakpoints were calculated exactly.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The arithmetic is exact.  Size-two blocks have \((w_l,q_l)=(1/(3k),1/4)\), size-four blocks have \((w_l,q_l)=(2/(3k),1/16)\), and
\[
 S=k\frac{1/(9k^2)}{1/4}
   +k\frac{4/(9k^2)}{1/16}=\frac{68}{9k},
 \qquad M=\frac{32}{3k}.
\]
Thus \(M\sqrt{\log(1/\alpha)}/\sqrt S
=32\sqrt{\log(1/\alpha)}/\sqrt{68k}\to0\).  The two breakpoints are \(3k/4\) and \(3k/32\), and \(q=2^{-r}\) makes it impossible for one common \(r\) to equal both two and four.  The finite-upper theorem proves the stated \(O(k^{-1/2})\) upper rate.  The matching minimax order remains conditional on the unresolved no-dominance lower bound.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Certify the claimed two-sided confidence-length order inherited from the no-dominance theorem.
open_obligations.obstruction: The algebraic reduction is complete, but the matching lower order uses the unresolved weighted-erasure spread result.
open_obligations.attempted: The identities for \(L,q,w,S,M\), the transformed no-dominance condition, and the finite-upper rate were derived exactly.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The partition identity gives \(L=n/r\), while balanced assignment and the weight definition give \(q_l=2^{-r}\) and \(w_l=r/n\).  Therefore
\[
 S=L\frac{w_l^2}{q_l}
 =\frac{r2^r}{n},\qquad
 M=\frac{w_l}{q_l}=\frac{r2^r}{n}=S.
\]
Squaring \(M\sqrt{\log(1/\alpha)}\le c_0\sqrt S\) gives
\[
 \frac{r2^r\log(1/\alpha)}n\le c_0^2.
\]
The finite-upper theorem consequently yields the asserted upper order with no extra extreme-confidence cutoff.  The matching lower order, and hence the full order statement in the target, remains dependent on the unresolved weighted-erasure posterior-spread lemma.

prose_updates.tldr: Unequal clique sizes turn full-neighborhood treatment and control exposure into independent nonidentical categorical reveals. The observed-data block Horvitz--Thompson estimator now has a fully derived clipped Bernstein interval, supported by a proved finite-product exponential lemma. The capped program has a certified water-filling optimizer and constant-factor trimming dual, and the trimmed observed-data interval gives the corresponding global upper bound. The exact hard-subexperiment embedding preserves all assignment ancillaries and arbitrary external interval randomization. The two all-procedure lower bounds remain open: the no-dominance tilted-sign posterior-spread lemma and the unrestricted smooth-location erasure lower bound. Consequently, the converse halves of the no-dominance frontier and the consistency boundary are not yet claimed. The pinned \(\texttt{szonszein/interference}\) version \(0.1.0\) diagnostic separately reports graph rejection and package-versus-reference label mismatch.

project_justification.gap: Existing partial-interference confidence procedures do not lower-bound expected length over every measurable externally randomized interval under fixed balanced assignment on unequal cliques. The remaining mathematical gap is now sharply localized: a biased weighted-Rademacher posterior-spread theorem under no dominance, and a smooth-location erasure lower bound with moving-support endpoint control in the capped regime.
project_justification.niche: The paper treats the known assignment distribution as the sole source of randomness and exposes two computable design scales: the quadratic rare-exposure scale for the implementable Bernstein interval and the capped water-filling or trimming scale when a block dominates. The optimizer and the trimming comparison are certified; their all-procedure minimax lower interpretation remains a stated open question.
project_justification.fill: The proved portion consists of the exact independent categorical block reduction, an observed-data Horvitz--Thompson estimator, a finite-sample clipped Bernstein interval, a bias-protected trimmed interval, a KKT-certified capped water-filling optimizer, a constant-factor trimming dual, and an exact Markov-kernel embedding covering randomized procedures. Exact six-block and two-scale calculations remain diagnostics. The note does not promote either unresolved erasure posterior-spread argument to a theorem.

prose_updates.related_work: TchetgenTchetgenVanderWeele2012, Section 4.3, derives finite-sample Hoeffding-type intervals for allocation-strategy effects under a two-stage partial-interference design, and RigdonHudgens2015 obtains exact confidence sets for those effects by randomization-test inversion. Those estimands and designs differ from the fixed unequal-clique All Treat versus All Control contrast here. AronowSamii2017 supplies the design--exposure--estimand architecture and exposure-specific inverse weighting, while UganderKarrerBackstromKleinberg2013 shows that full-neighborhood exposure probabilities may be exponentially small in degree. BasseAiroldi2018 gives a nonconcentration warning, UganderYin2023 changes the design to mitigate small probabilities, and KandirosHarshawSavje2026 studies design-based mean-squared-error criteria rather than all-interval confidence length. CaiLow2004 and ArmstrongKolesar2018 motivate modulus logic in Gaussian experiments, but do not prove the weighted nonidentical erasure posterior-spread result needed here. The present proved additions are self-contained finite-product concentration and capped-optimization or trimming certificates; neither is used as a substitute for the still-open randomized-interval lower bounds. The pinned \(\texttt{szonszein/interference}\) version \(0.1.0\) source uses the complement of All Treat in its second output column, so the diagnostic compares it with an independently recomputed unanimous All Control reference.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The finite-product concentration lemma, clipped interval, trimmed upper interval, capped optimizer, and trimming dual are proved. The hard-subexperiment lemma also settles only the experiment-to-experiment bridge: it reconstructs unrevealed assignments and transfers coverage and expected length without discarding ancillaries. The no-dominance lower frontier still requires a biased weighted-Rademacher concentration-function bound carrying the exact conditional variance factors \(1-t^2s_l^2\), followed by posterior missed-mass calculations in both conditional-noise regimes. The unrestricted lower frontier separately requires a smooth-location erasure construction with explicit moving-support endpoint control and a justified likelihood or Hellinger-to-posterior-spread conversion. Until those arguments close, neither the two-sided minimax frontier nor the reverse implication in the consistency boundary is established.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The proved results concern fixed outcomes in \([-1/2,1/2]\), known unequal disjoint clique blocks, and independent unit-level \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) assignment. The estimator and both upper intervals are measurable from \(D\) and known design quantities. The capped water-filling optimizer and its constant-factor relation to trimming are certified. Arbitrary external interval randomization is preserved by the exact lower-experiment embedding, but the required posterior-spread inequalities are still open. Therefore the no-dominance and unrestricted minimax lower bounds, the full consistency equivalence, and the two-sided equal- and two-scale rate corollaries remain unproved. The statement that \(S\to0\) is not necessary is nevertheless supported by an explicit valid clique triangular array and the proved trimmed upper bound. Overlapping or nonclique neighborhoods are rejected before the software diagnostic reports an interval.

statement_notes.justification: The capped optimizer and trimming dual are now proved; this question is retained solely for the matching all-measurable randomized-interval lower bound.
statement_notes.gap: A smooth-location weighted-erasure lower bound still needs moving-support endpoint control and a rigorous conversion from likelihood or Hellinger bounds to posterior interval spread.
statement_notes.consumer: Closing this question would turn the proved dominance-aware upper modulus into a two-sided minimax confidence-length frontier.

statement_notes.justification: The computable equivalence \(\omega_\alpha\to0\Longleftrightarrow\rho_0\to0\) and the sufficient implication to vanishing risk are proved.
statement_notes.gap: The reverse implication from vanishing minimax risk to vanishing modulus remains exactly the unresolved unrestricted erasure lower bound.
statement_notes.consumer: Once the lower bound closes, designers obtain the full intrinsic consistency boundary; before then, the proved trimming criterion is a sufficient design certificate.
